clade_name: unverified (data-derived similarity clusters, not published Alpha/Beta genera)
conclusion: Risk label is almost perfectly confounded with sequence-similarity cluster: at every tested resolution only one cluster mixes high- and low-risk types, so most leave-one-cluster-out folds are degenerate (single-class test, or removing the mixed cluster leaves training single-class). Evaluable folds exist only at k=10 (1 fold, held-out 16|30|31|33|35|51|52|56|58|73|82 -> AUC 0.955) and k=12 (1 fold, 30|51|56|82 -> AUC 1.000). Two informative folds are not enough to claim phylogenetic generalization; the type-level model is effectively a clade-membership proxy and must be reframed as a descriptive clade-level physicochemical signature, or re-labelled with variant-level phenotypes.
